description:

This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

Kairos Power is seeking a Buyer III to support procurement activities across Kairos Power, with a primary focus on raw material purchasing for manufacturing operations. In this role, you will partner closely with Manufacturing, Planning, Material Handling, Engineering, suppliers, and Supply Chain & Procurement (SC&P) to support material readiness, manage supplier performance, and resolve supply issues.

We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their work, communicates openly, builds strong relationships, and is comfortable learning in an evolving manufacturing environment. The successful candidate will be supported in developing deep knowledge of Kairos' raw material supplier base and manufacturing requirements while contributing ideas and improvements as their expertise grows.

Responsibilities

  • Manage the full procurement lifecycle for assigned raw material commodities and support general procurement activities across Kairos Power as needed, including RFQs, purchase order placement, supplier communication, and order management.
  • Serve as the primary procurement point of contact for assigned raw material commodities, partnering closely with Manufacturing, Material Handling, Planning, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and SC&P leadership to support production readiness and resolve supply issues.
  • Develop expertise in Kairos’ raw material program requirements, supplier capabilities, manufacturing requirements, and Kairos’ procurement processes to support effective and timely purchasing decisions.
  • Organize and prioritize assigned procurement activities, monitor supplier commitments, proactively communicate risks and changing priorities, and work collaboratively with teammates and stakeholders to drive timely resolution of supply issues.
  • Obtain and evaluate supplier quotations, analyze commercial terms, support negotiations, and ensure purchase orders are accurate, compliant, and aligned with company policies and contractual requirements.
  • Analyze supplier performance and procurement data to identify opportunities to improve supplier reliability, inform inventory decisions, reduce risk, and support manufacturing objectives.
  • Build trusted relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders through clear, responsive communication while serving as a knowledgeable procurement resource and supporting knowledge sharing within the team.
  • Proactively identify and implement practical improvements to procurement processes, supplier management practices, and cross-functional workflows that improve efficiency, scalability, and manufacturing support.
  • Prepare and communicate procurement status, supplier performance, and material risk updates to internal stakeholders and leadership.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • 4+ years of procurement, purchasing, or sourcing experience; candidates considered at the Buyer III level should demonstrate greater independent judgment, ownership, and experience with moderately complex procurement activities.
  • Experience supporting manufacturing operations through procurement, purchasing, sourcing, materials, or supply chain activities.
  • Experience managing supplier relationships, purchase orders, RFQs, and commercial purchasing activities.
  • Direct experience purchasing raw materials or production-critical manufacturing commodities is highly preferred; experience with metals, alloys, industrial materials, or similar manufacturing commodities is a plus.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with Manufacturing, Planning, Material Handling, Engineering, Operations, or similar internal stakeholders.
  • Experience using ERP or procurement systems such as Coupa, SAP, Oracle, Ariba, or equivalent.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Working knowledge of the procurement lifecycle, including supplier identification, RFQs, commercial evaluation, purchase order management, and supplier performance management.
  • Strong self-organization and prioritization skills with the ability to manage multiple procurement activities, follow through on commitments, and adapt to changing manufacturing and business priorities.
  • Apply analytical problem-solving skills and initiative to investigate unfamiliar or ambiguous procurement issues, use available information and resources, exercise sound judgment, and seek input when needed.
  • Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to create and maintain effective relationships with suppliers, teammates, and cross-functional partners.
  • Demonstrates integrity, positive intent, and respect in working relationships; communicates directly and constructively, actively listens, raises questions when needed, and welcomes feedback and differing perspectives.
  • Openness to learning new commodities, manufacturing processes, supplier capabilities, and internal systems, with the ability to quickly apply new knowledge and expand procurement capability.
  • Ability to analyze supplier and procurement data, identify risks, and recommend practical actions that improve cost, schedule, quality, or reliability.
  • Bring a proactive, continuous-improvement mindset by identifying practical opportunities to strengthen procurement processes, supplier management practices, and cross-functional ways of working.
  • Ability to proactively collect, document, manage, and share procurement knowledge across the team.
  • Demonstrate a mission-centered and responsible approach by understanding how procurement work supports Kairos Power's goals, delivering on commitments, using resources thoughtfully, and maintaining strong safety expectations.
  • Ability to evaluate supplier quotations and commercial terms, assess cost and business tradeoffs, and support supplier negotiations.
  • Ability to interpret and apply procurement policies, purchase order requirements, and applicable contractual terms in purchasing activities.

Job Summary

The Reactor Systems department is seeking a highly accomplished Distinguished Engineer to provide senior technical leadership across reactor system design, integration, analysis, testing, qualification, and deployment for Kairos Power’s fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor technology. This role will establish the long-term technical vision, engineering strategy, and architectural direction for reactor systems to ensure that reactor system designs meet safety, performance, quality, manufacturability, maintainability, and deployment objectives.

The Distinguished Engineer provides independent technical leadership across multiple engineering organizations, shaping reactor system architecture, design philosophy, engineering standards and technical strategy for Kairos Power’s advanced reactor program. This individual serves as a trusted technical advisor to executive leadership, resolves the organization’s most complex technical challenges, and influences technical decisions supporting commercialization of Kairos Power’s reactor technology.

Responsibilities

  • Provide technical authority to shape the long-term technical vision, system architecture, and engineering strategy for Reactor Systems consistent with Kairos Power’s commercialization roadmap.
  • Serve as the highest-level technical authority for reactor systems design philosophy, integration strategy, and technical decision-making.
  • Drive enterprise-wide technical consistency across reactor systems design, integration, analysis, testing, qualification, and deployment activities.
  • Guide development and oversight of reactor system architecture, system requirements, design bases, interface definitions, verification plans, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Lead resolution of complex cross-disciplinary technical issues involving reactor vessel systems, reactor internals, auxiliary systems, nuclear design, design margin, thermal hydraulics, safety analysis, I&C, manufacturing, testing, licensing, and operations.
  • Develop engineering standards, technical methodologies, design principles, and best practices that improve engineering quality and organizational effectiveness.
  • Influence corporate technology strategy through collaboration with executive leadership and engineering management teams.
  • Identify emerging technical risks and opportunities affecting reactor technology development and commercialization.
  • Communicate complex technical issues and provide direction on key design trades, technical decisions, requirements allocation, system interfaces, and design margins affecting reactor system performance and safety.
  • Lead or support major design integration reviews to ensure structures, systems, and components are compatible, accessible for installation and maintenance, and aligned with safety, construction, and lifecycle requirements.
  • Prepare and review reactor systems design documentation and supporting engineering analyses, including design descriptions, drawings, test plans, reports, specifications, calculations, design decision records, thermal/structural/system analyses, FMEAs, hazard analyses, and design margin assessments.
  • Maintain knowledge of and assess compliance with applicable codes and standards such as ASME, ANSI, ASTM, ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, and other relevant industry standards.
  • Assist in cost, schedule, and risk assessments related to reactor system design, testing, fabrication, integration, and deployment activities.
  • Mentor engineers across Reactor Systems and adjacent technical teams, including coaching on design rigor, engineering judgment, documentation quality, and cross-functional integration.
  • Represent Reactor Systems in high-impact technical discussions, design reviews, readiness reviews, audits, and executive-level technical briefings.
  • Promote a strong engineering culture focused on safety, technical excellence, accountability, clarity, and efficient execution.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related technical discipline is required.
  • 20+ years of progressively increasing technical leadership experience in nuclear reactor design, reactor systems engineering, advanced technology development, complex mechanical systems, high-temperature systems, or similarly regulated engineering environments is required.
  • Demonstrated experience leading major technical scope across complex engineering programs, preferably involving nuclear, energy, chemical, oil and gas, or power generation systems is required.
  • Recognized technical authority with demonstrated contributions to the advancement of advanced reactor technology, complex engineered systems, or related engineering disciplines through technical leadership, publications, patents, standards development, invited presentations, or equivalent achievements preferred.
  • Experience working within formal configuration management, design control, or product lifecycle management systems under a recognized quality program such as ASME NQA-1, ISO 9001, or equivalent is desired.
  • Experience with applicable codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII Division 1 and 2, Section III Division 5, ANSI, ASTM, ASME Y14.5, or related standards is desired.
  • Experience participating in or leading formal technical reviews, readiness reviews, design reviews, or safety-related engineering reviews.
  • Experience communicating complex technical issues to executive, regulatory, quality, manufacturing, operations, or cross-functional stakeholders.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Recognized expert capable of defining technical vision and engineering strategy across multiple engineering disciplines.
  • Strong understanding of advanced reactor technology, high-temperature systems, molten salt systems, reactor vessel systems, reactor internals, auxiliary systems, and safety-significant mechanical components.
  • Knowledge of high-temperature design considerations, including thermal stress, creep-fatigue, irradiation effects, material compatibility, and component degradation mechanisms.
  • Ability to establish long-term technical vision and guide engineering organizations toward successful execution of complex technology roadmaps.
  • Ability to influence technical direction without organizational authority and align long-term technology strategy with business objectives.
  • Ability to interpret and apply industry codes and standards, including ASME, ANSI, ASTM, and ASME BPVC.
  • Ability to evaluate enterprise-level technical tradeoffs involving safety, manufacturing, operability, licensing, economics, and commercialization.
  • Familiarity with 3D CAD design tools such as SolidWorks, AVEVA, or equivalent, and engineering analysis tools for thermal and structural modeling.

  • Ability to evaluate design maturity, technical readiness, test adequacy, and verification strategy for first-of-a-kind reactor systems.
  • Strong analytical problem-solving abilities to resolve complex design issues efficiently.

Job Summary

Kairos Power is seeking a highly skilled, self-directed Quality Control Technician to perform complex inspections of precision-machined parts, fabricated components, and assemblies supporting nuclear technology development and manufacturing. This role requires advanced dimensional metrology expertise, strong manufacturing knowledge, and sound judgment when verifying components whose conformance is critical to safety, performance, and nuclear quality requirements.

The successful candidate will independently plan and execute inspections, maintain consistently high productivity, and produce accurate, traceable inspection records. They will take ownership of assigned work, anticipate and resolve inspection challenges, and communicate risks early. As a senior technical contributor, this individual will support inspection planning, mentor other inspectors, and work closely with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to improve inspection effectiveness while maintaining rigorous acceptance standards.

Responsibilities

  • Independently plan, prioritize, and execute complex dimensional inspections, taking ownership from initial drawing review through completion of inspection records and communication of results.
  • Inspect precision-machined parts, fabricated components, and assemblies for dimensional, geometric, and visual conformance to approved drawings, specifications, and inspection plans.

  • Interpret complex GD&T requirements, establish appropriate datum reference frames, and select measurement methods suited to feature tolerances, part geometry, and required accuracy.

  • Align 3D CAD models and measurement data to specified drawing datums, ensuring alignment methods accurately represent design requirements.
  • Evaluate fixturing, accessibility, temperature, part condition, and measurement uncertainty when establishing inspection methods and assessing results.
  • Support development and validation of in-machine probing routines for 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis machining centers, including correlation with independent inspection methods where required.
  • Partner with manufacturing to validate setups, evaluate process capability, and troubleshoot dimensional discrepancies.
  • Perform inspections supporting nuclear quality requirements with disciplined adherence to approved procedures, required hold points, traceability, and documentation controls.
  • Verify drawing and model revisions, component identification, and measurement equipment calibration status before performing inspections.
  • Recognize ambiguous requirements, questionable measurements, and potential nonconformances; pause affected inspection or acceptance activities and escalate for resolution.
  • Document nonconformances objectively and preserve relevant measurement data. Verify acceptance only within assigned authority and after required dispositions or approvals are complete.
  • Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to investigate root causes, implement corrective actions, and verify their effectiveness.
  • Provide design-for-inspectability feedback during design reviews, including recommendations on datum schemes, tolerances, inspection access, and measurement methods.
  • Maintain high inspection throughput through effective preparation, programming, sequencing, and coordination. Communicate workload constraints and schedule risks early.
  • Improve inspection efficiency by developing repeatable methods, reusable programs, and appropriate gauging or fixtures while preserving measurement reliability.
  • Serve as a technical resource and mentor for other inspectors, supporting training, troubleshooting, and consistency in inspection practices.
  • Support internal, customer, and external audits by providing complete inspection records and clearly explaining inspection methods and results.
  • Maintain a safe, clean, and organized work environment and protect inspection equipment from damage or misuse.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required; technical training, apprenticeship; an associate’s degree in metrology, manufacturing, machining, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years of progressively responsible experience in dimensional inspection, precision manufacturing quality control, or a closely related field; or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated experience independently completing complex inspections and producing complete, accurate inspection documentation with minimal supervision.
  • Advanced proficiency interpreting engineering drawings and applying GD&T in accordance with ASME Y14.5.
  • Proficiency with precision measurement instruments, including micrometers, calipers, height gauges, bore gauges, indicators, and surface plates.
  • Demonstrated proficiency programming and operating at least one advanced dimensional measurement system, such as a CMM, portable measurement arm, or laser tracker.
  • Experience with dimensional inspection software such as Verisurf, PolyWorks, PC-DMIS, or comparable software. Experience with Romer arms and laser trackers preferred.
  • Strong working knowledge of machining processes, fixturing, and manufacturing variation.
  • Experience inspecting complex geometries, tight-tolerance features, large components, or assemblies with challenging datum relationships.
  • Experience working within a controlled quality management system with formal inspection, traceability, and nonconformance requirements.
  • Experience inspecting nuclear components or other high-consequence hardware in aerospace, defense, or similarly demanding manufacturing environments strongly preferred.
  • Experience with in-machine probing software and inspection routines for multiaxis machining centers preferred.
  • Experience with ERP systems, digital inspection records, first article inspection reports, and audit support preferred.
  • Relevant certification, such as ASQ Certified Quality Inspector, Certified Quality Technician, or GD&T certification, preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Ability to develop inspection plans and select appropriate measurement methods based on drawing requirements, feature geometry, tolerances, accessibility, and required accuracy.
  • Working knowledge of configuration and revision control practices for drawings, models, inspection programs, and inspection records.
  • Ability to verify the suitability and calibration status of measurement equipment and recognize conditions that may affect measurement validity.
  • Advanced proficiency interpreting engineering drawings and applying GD&T in accordance with ASME Y14.5.
  • Proficiency with precision measurement instruments, including micrometers, calipers, height gauges, bore gauges, indicators, and surface plates.
  • Ability to organize work, identify next steps, resolve routine obstacles, and follow assignments through to completion with minimal direction.
  • Ability to maintain a high volume of accurate, complete inspection work through preparation, efficient measurement strategies, and disciplined time management.
  • Ability to recognize when results require additional verification, when a method is unsuitable, and when work must pause for technical clarification or quality review.
  • Strong understanding of datum establishment, alignment strategies, measurement uncertainty, repeatability, reproducibility, and the limitations of inspection equipment.
  • Ability to raise concerns and maintain acceptance standards under schedule pressure, with a clear understanding of personal qualification and approval limits.
  • Ability to distinguish component variation from setup, programming, alignment, or measurement errors and develop practical approaches to resolve discrepancies.
  • Ability to produce inspection records that clearly connect the inspected component, applicable requirements, measurement results, equipment used, and acceptance status.
  • Ability to explain technical findings clearly to inspectors, machinists, engineers, and leadership and communicate risks early enough to support action.
  • Ability to mentor others, share knowledge, and improve inspection consistency without requiring formal supervisory authority.
  • Ability to identify and implement practical improvements that reduce inspection time, rework, and avoidable delays.
  • Understanding of ISO 9001 quality management principles and the ability to learn and apply applicable nuclear quality program requirements.
  • Working knowledge of statistical process control, process capability, and measurement system analysis.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and commitment to safety.

Physical Demands

Reporting directly to the Head of Reactor Systems, the position will support the development of reactor vessel hardware and interfaces, including the vessel shell, penetrations, supports, closures, structural interfaces, and related mechanical components. Responsibilities

  • Own and manage design scope for reactor vessel components, interfaces, and hardware packages.
  • Develop and maintain reactor vessel requirements, design bases, interface definitions, verification plans, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Lead the mechanical design and technical execution of assigned reactor vessel structures, components, and interfaces, ensuring compliance with system requirements and design objectives.

Job Summary

Kairos Power is seeking a highly motivated Senior Mechanical Engineer focused on Remote Handling Special Components with expertise in modular hardware design for remotely operated systems.

This role is centered on the design, physical integration, and demonstration of remote handling technologies through full-scale mockups and prototype builds. The Senior Engineer will drive 1:1 scale integration efforts to validate interfaces, clearances, tolerances, and handling sequences—systematically derisking reactor maintenance strategies prior to deployment.

This position integrates remote handling requirements directly into component architecture and system interfaces to enable efficient assembly, maintenance, inspection, and long-term operability. The role emphasizes hands-on engineering, rapid build-test cycles, and cross-functional collaboration in a highly regulated environment.

Responsibilities

Modular Maintenance System Development

  • Apply lifecycle design principles including maintainability, inspectability, and decommissioning
  • Integrate remote handling requirements into hardware architecture and system interfaces
  • Develop and maintain interface control documentation supporting plant-level integration
  • Design, build, and evaluate 1:1 scale mockups and integration test articles to validate handling concepts
  • Develop structured test plans and acceptance criteria for full-scale demonstrations
  • Coordinate test readiness reviews with QA and Systems Engineering
  • Implement design updates based on mockup results, demonstrations, and operational feedback
  • Support project planning and cost estimation for integration and testing activities
  • Interface with vendors to ensure manufacturability and feasibility of specialized components
  • Conduct risk and reliability assessments for maintenance systems

Remote Handling Solutions

  • Develop remote handling hardware enabling efficient component repair and replacement
  • Lead hands-on design-build-test cycles to mature handling approaches
  • Execute full-scale integration mockups to validate reach, clearances, tooling alignment, ergonomics, and sequencing

  • Identify integration risks early and mitigate through rapid prototyping and physical demonstration

Testing and Validation

  • Align demonstration opportunities with reactor and facility schedules
  • Develop execution plans for rapid, high-value physical demonstrations
  • Support inspections, installations, shakedown, tuning, and commissioning activities

Collaboration

  • Partner with engineering, laboratory, shop, and materials teams to execute accelerated hardware development

Engineering Reports

  • Publish engineering reports documenting design details, mockup results, and integration findings

Team Contribution

  • Share technical knowledge and best practices across the organization
  • Mentor junior engineers in hardware design, integration, and prototype testing

Other duties as assigned

Kairos Power is seeking a highly capable Test Engineer to support the design, development, and operation of experimental hardware, laboratory infrastructure, and first-of-a-kind test systems supporting advanced reactor technology.
